as_told.title: Sculptor Michael Richards' plane sculptures and death in the Twin Towers
as_told.place_text: Miami; World Trade Center, New York

plain: This story is about an artist who worked in a studio inside the World Trade Center towers in New York in 2001. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells it first. He says the towers had an art programme, and one resident artist made a picture of himself as a Tuskegee Airman, a wartime pilot, with old fighter planes all flying into him, twelve days before the attacks of September 11, 2001, when hijacked planes struck the towers. A writer on dreams and seeing the future, Eric Wargo, tells the same story on two later episodes and fills it in. He names the artist as Michael Richards and calls the work a sculpture, titled Tar Baby vs. St. Sebastian. Wargo says a group called the Lower Manhattan Cultural Council gave studios to groups of fifteen artists for six months at a time. He says Richards alone among them stayed in his studio the night of September 10 and was killed the next morning. Wargo puts this in his book Time Loops, and the story is told as an example of art that seems to see its maker's own future.
